title: Elgar’s finale before and after the cuts
work: Cello Concerto in E minor, Op. 85 — a shared passage from the finale
question: How do Harrison and Elgar shape the finale’s retained moving passage beside the complete Skidmore performance?
intro: Harrison and Elgar’s 1919–20 acoustic recording compresses the whole concerto onto four sides issued in 1921; the Skidmore file contains only the complete finale. The comparison deliberately aligns just 85–124 seconds of Skidmore with 710–745 seconds of the already-joined Harrison stream, a continuous early-finale overlap rather than music on opposite sides of a cut. Its median chroma confidence is 0.950, but the timing remains provisional and the acoustic transfer changes which details of cello and orchestra are audible. Neither the full-file durations nor this short overlap establish Elgar’s tempo for the omitted music.
